milestones.title: v0.0.1
milestones.description: Core engineering foundation: live pods, navigation, details, logs, exec and qualified local installation. No public 0.0.1 release is promised; first public activation is 0.1.0 under D10.

milestones.title: v0.1.0
milestones.description: Standard resource families, safe workload mutations, editing, port forwarding, standalone executables, and performance qualification. First usable public phase after core/workload, standalone, performance and terminal-history qualification; activation remains owner-reviewed D10.

milestones.title: v0.2.0
milestones.description: Configurable themes, navigation/resource views, external plugins, deliberate configuration/secret workflows, context and completed-pod cleanup, custom-resource jumps and verified Homebrew bottles. Retains generic CRDs and aggregate logs from 0.1.0.

milestones.title: v0.3.0
milestones.description: Foundations and quality: decompose the application shell, decouple tests, retain the tested framework compatibility pin, degrade gracefully on large clusters, enforce offline startup budgets, measure advisory 0.x UI startup, reach kubeconfig parity with kubectl, add error boundaries and fast test tiers, and rewrite the documentation. Framework cleanup and strict UI startup qualification remain stable-release work. No new feature families.

milestones.title: v0.4.0
milestones.description: Observability: metrics-server and Prometheus metrics with terminal charts, cluster overview, relationships, RBAC analysis, diagnostics, sanitized exports, curated views for every remaining Lens resource family and container environment inspection. Requires its qualifier and every earlier phase.

milestones.title: v0.5.0
milestones.description: Operations: full Helm lifecycle, local manifests and Kustomize, resource templates, node shell, cordon/drain, ephemeral debugging, HTTP benchmarks and policy/quota/admission exploration. Requires its qualifier and every earlier phase.

milestones.title: v0.6.0
milestones.description: Multi-cluster workspace: cluster catalog and pinned hotbar, multi-cluster views, context-scoped local terminals, cloud cluster discovery, curated CRD and GitOps packs, change timeline and diffs, native exec/port-forward transport. Requires its qualifier and every earlier phase.

milestones.title: v0.7.0
milestones.description: Ecosystem and intelligence: stable in-process Python extension API, extension index, security center, read-only MCP server and opt-in bring-your-own AI assistant. Requires its qualifier and every earlier phase.

milestones.title: v0.8.0
milestones.description: Platforms and accessibility: Windows terminal and packaged installation, shell completion, OCI image, distribution recipes, advanced embedded-terminal input and accessibility. Requires its qualifier and every earlier phase.

milestones.title: v0.9.0
milestones.description: Release candidate: configuration and extension API freeze, compatibility matrix, versioned documentation, K9s and Lens parity dry run and stabilization. Requires its qualifier and every earlier phase.

milestones.title: v1.0.0
milestones.description: Stable release: every phase complete, including Windows; stable configuration and extension contracts; evidence-backed Kubernetes and platform compatibility; audited capability parity with K9s and Lens (open source and publicly documented Pro features), with every difference documented.

epics.title: Kubernetes sessions, discovery, and live state
epics.outcome: Maintain correct resource state across context changes, API failures, pagination, watches, and custom resources.

epics.title: Terminal resource browsing and navigation
epics.outcome: Deliver responsive resource tables, predictable keyboard navigation, useful details, and generic resource views.

epics.title: Logs and interactive sessions
epics.outcome: Provide reliable logs, container shells, and managed port forwarding with explicit targets and cleanup.

epics.title: Safe workload and configuration operations
epics.outcome: Implement useful Kubernetes writes with read-only enforcement, clear targets, validation, conflict handling, and tested outcomes.

epics.title: Themes, configuration, and plugins
epics.outcome: Let users customize appearance, navigation, columns, and external commands through documented, validated contracts.

epics.title: Observability and troubleshooting
epics.outcome: Connect metrics, events, resource relationships, and permission evidence into practical troubleshooting workflows.

epics.title: Advanced cluster operations
epics.outcome: Add node maintenance, diagnostic sessions, and bounded service benchmarks with predictable cleanup and disruption handling.

epics.title: Packaging, installation, and release delivery
epics.outcome: Publish tested immutable releases through PyPI, Homebrew, and standalone downloads with reproducible provenance and upgrade paths.

epics.title: Integration, performance, and compatibility qualification
epics.outcome: Validate real API/terminal behavior, bounded resources, supported versions, and the stable product contract.

epics.title: User documentation and contribution experience
epics.outcome: Keep installation and user guidance accurate, then publish a versioned documentation website after the core product ships.

epics.title: Extended platforms, accessibility and ecosystem delivery
epics.outcome: Track the full upstream installation surface without implying that external registries have accepted a package.

epics.title: Foundations and engineering quality
epics.outcome: A codebase that can absorb Lens-class features: small units, behavior-level tests, fast feedback, no private framework dependencies, large-cluster resilience, instant startup and kubeconfig parity.

epics.title: Multi-cluster workspace beyond Lens
epics.outcome: Match the Lens catalog, hotbar and terminal in the terminal, then go further with multi-cluster views, change timelines and native transport.

epics.title: Ecosystem and intelligence
epics.outcome: Python-native extensibility, a free security center and optional AI help that never leaks secrets.

tasks.title: Prepare repository governance and the complete implementation backlog
tasks.scope: Prepare the public Apache-2.0 repository, planning documents, issue hierarchy, project, author identity, and protected contribution workflow before application implementation.
acceptance: README states the planning stage and briefly credits K9s; architecture, quality, release, and distribution decisions are checked in.
Every planned task has an epic, milestone, priority, acceptance criteria, verification, and explicit blockers; the dependency graph is acyclic.
Git author email is repository-local, initial docs pass checks, main is protected, and the source repository is public under #155 while the separate project remains private.
tasks.verification: Verify GitHub state, documentation links, planning data, CI, SSH push, and repository-local Git identity. No application release is created.

tasks.title: Bootstrap the installable Python package and developer toolchain
tasks.scope: Create the src/kuberich package, Hatchling build metadata, argparse entry point, uv lockfile, and supported Python matrix.
acceptance: Project/import/CLI names are kuberich; pyproject.toml owns the version; --help and --version work from an installed wheel.
Released Textual and kubernetes_asyncio dependencies are pinned by uv.lock; the declared Python range matches tested versions.
Dev commands and package assets are configured; the initial CLI reports its actual limited capability without fake cluster data.
tasks.verification: Run clean uv sync, CLI behavior tests, Ruff, strict mypy, build/metadata validation, and wheel installation on Python 3.12-3.14.

tasks.title: Enforce independent coverage and required application CI gates
tasks.scope: Replace the planning-only quality stage with required application verification before feature work.
acceptance: CI measures all production modules and independently fails below 90% lines or 90% branches; changed-line coverage is at least 90%.
Critical deterministic modules have a maintained 100% gate; tests and broad exclusions cannot inflate production coverage.

Ruff, format, strict mypy, tests, build, and the aggregate quality gate reject failures, cancellation, or invalid skips. During approved private GitHub Free development, the maintainer verifies every check before merging; automatic branch protection is required before first public release (D04).
tasks.verification: Use controlled failing fixtures/temporary changes to demonstrate each gate rejects regressions; verify coverage artifacts and Linux/macOS CI.

tasks.title: Implement validated configuration and sanitized diagnostics
tasks.scope: Add platform-appropriate settings, a versioned YAML schema, application errors, and useful local diagnostics.
acceptance: Configuration has typed defaults, atomic writes, explicit precedence, invalid-value errors, and forward-compatible unknown-field handling.
No configuration operation changes kubeconfig current-context; missing configuration starts with documented defaults.
Logs rotate and redact credentials; CLI errors have stable exit behavior and concise user messages; debug details stay outside terminal rendering.
tasks.verification: Test missing/malformed files, interrupted writes, migrations, path handling, permissions, log bounds, and redaction with temporary directories.

tasks.title: Define and test Kubernetes, plugin, and terminal trust boundaries
tasks.scope: Write the focused threat model and implement shared input/redaction/target primitives needed by the first workflows.
acceptance: Document trust boundaries for kubeconfig exec credentials, API fields, logs, terminal controls, subprocesses, plugins, and release artifacts.
Shared helpers escape untrusted markup/control sequences and redact credentials without hiding actionable error context.
Mutation/command target identities are immutable snapshots; tests never silently use a developer cluster; secret fixtures are synthetic.
tasks.verification: Exercise hostile names/log controls, credential-bearing errors, target capture, and unsafe test-context rejection; critical helpers meet 100% coverage.

tasks.title: Create isolated kubeconfig and context sessions
tasks.scope: Implement explicit asynchronous clients and context/namespace selection without global configuration mutation.
acceptance: Load explicit/default kubeconfig paths and supported credential mechanisms with TLS verification on by default.
Each context owns its API session, namespace, and generation; context selection does not rewrite user kubeconfig.
Unavailable credentials, forbidden namespace listing, timeouts, and disconnected clusters produce distinct actionable states.
tasks.verification: Test multiple contexts, credential-exec contracts, invalid certificates, missing config, restricted RBAC, and session closure using fake endpoints.

tasks.title: Implement API discovery and consistent paginated resource listing
tasks.scope: Provide discovery and normalized resource snapshots for the initial pod/namespace/detail workflows.
acceptance: Distinguish namespaced and cluster-scoped endpoints; discover supported verbs and API groups instead of assuming universal access.
Follow continue tokens while preserving the collection snapshot/resourceVersion and normalize typed display data separately from raw manifests.
Handle partial discovery and forbidden requests explicitly; expose list resourceVersion for the watch engine.
tasks.verification: Contract-test empty/multiple pages, expired pagination, denied groups, malformed responses, and correct namespace scoping.

tasks.title: Implement resilient list-watch synchronization
tasks.scope: Maintain live resource state using the initial collection version and a recoverable watch stream.
acceptance: Apply ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED and BOOKMARK events idempotently with stable UID identity and opaque resourceVersion handling.
Recover timeouts/EOF/retryable transport failures with bounded backoff and jitter; relist on expired versions/410.
Permission failures are surfaced without hot retry loops; stream and queue lifetimes are bounded and cancellable.
tasks.verification: Use deterministic fake-server/clock tests for list-watch gaps, duplicates, deletion/recreation, 410, reconnect, permission denial, and cancellation.

tasks.title: Own session cancellation and reject stale-context updates
tasks.scope: Connect session lifecycle, resource state, and view subscriptions with explicit cleanup.
acceptance: Context/namespace/resource switches cancel and await obsolete work and reject late results with generation checks.
UI subscriptions observe bounded state updates; inactive resources do not accumulate unbounded watches.
Disconnected/stale status is visible and recovery replaces the correct snapshot; exit leaves no owned tasks or sessions.
tasks.verification: Race-test rapid switches, late pages/events, cancelled reconnects, repeated opening/closing, and task/session leak detection.

tasks.title: Support dynamic custom resource discovery and version selection
tasks.scope: Extend the adapter contract to arbitrary accessible resource types and CRDs.
acceptance: Resolve group/version/resource and scope from discovery, including preferred versions and ambiguous short-name handling.
Custom resources support generic list/watch/get and server-provided Table metadata with a graceful fallback.
Discovery refresh handles installed/removed CRDs and inaccessible API groups without breaking core views.
tasks.verification: Test namespaced/cluster CRDs, version changes, alias collisions, missing Table responses, and restricted discovery on a disposable cluster.

tasks.title: Build the Textual application shell and responsive layout
tasks.scope: Create the real terminal shell with header, resource region, command/filter inputs, status, and contextual help.
acceptance: The header always identifies context/namespace and connection state; the main view starts without an artificial splash delay.
Keyboard focus, mouse selection, Escape/back, help, and narrow-window layouts behave consistently.
Normal handlers do not block the event loop; styles are packaged assets and the app restores terminal state on exit.
tasks.verification: Use Pilot tests at small/normal/large sizes for focus, navigation, resize, errors, and clean shutdown; add limited layout snapshots.

tasks.title: Implement the live pod table with stable selection and typed sorting
tasks.scope: Render live resource snapshots incrementally with meaningful pod/container health columns.
acceptance: Rows use stable identity; updates preserve selection and scroll position and do not rebuild the whole table per event.
Readiness, restarts, age, waiting/termination reasons, and pod status are derived accurately; typed sorting is numeric/chronological.
Horizontal/vertical scrolling and deletion of a selected object have deterministic behavior; empty/error/loading states differ.
tasks.verification: Test updates while sorting/scrolling, selected deletion/recreation, init/multi-container statuses, quantity ordering, and Unicode width.

tasks.title: Add resource commands, filtering, namespace shortcuts, and help
tasks.scope: Provide keyboard-first command navigation and filtering with discoverable actions.
acceptance: Colon commands and resource aliases navigate accessible views; slash filtering supports documented text/regex modes and clear invalid-pattern errors.
Namespace/context selection and navigation history preserve the intended view state without stale updates.
Contextual help matches actual bindings and available actions; typing/filtering cannot accidentally invoke destructive bindings.
tasks.verification: Pilot-test command completion/unknown commands, invalid regex, namespace changes, focus routing, and history restoration.

tasks.title: Show YAML, resource details, and related events
tasks.scope: Add useful read-only inspection of the selected resource and its warning events.
acceptance: YAML preserves API field names and omits presentation-only fields; secrets remain hidden in ordinary views.
Details and related events retain the captured resource/context identity and show permission/unavailable errors clearly.
Search, scroll, copy of non-sensitive content, and return-to-table preserve navigation state.
Support managedFields visibility and text search; describe renders resource-specific evidence without exposing secret values.
tasks.verification: Test field serialization, event association, stale selection, access denial, redaction, markup escaping, and viewer navigation.

tasks.title: Add standard workload, networking, and storage resource views
tasks.scope: Extend the resource registry with deployments, replica/stateful/daemon sets, jobs/cronjobs, services/endpoints, ingress, configmaps, secrets, nodes, PVCs/PVs, and storage classes.
acceptance: Each advertised resource has a functional discovered endpoint, scoped list/watch/detail support, and meaningful typed columns.
Supported actions are resource-specific; inaccessible or absent APIs are presented accurately.
Registry definitions are reusable and tested; the UI does not require a new large screen class for each resource.
tasks.verification: Use parameterized registry/column contracts and kind fixtures covering workload, network, storage, batch, and cluster-scoped resources.

tasks.title: Deliver generic CRD tables and configurable resource columns
tasks.scope: Make dynamically discovered resources browsable with useful server and fallback columns.
acceptance: Generic resource navigation supports CRDs, scope, aliases, version identity, and raw YAML/details.
Use server-provided columns when available, with stable fallback columns and typed sorting.
Removed schemas, unknown fields, and column configuration errors preserve a usable view.
tasks.verification: Pilot and integration tests cover namespaced/cluster CRDs, server Table fallback, discovery refresh, and malformed column values.

tasks.title: Implement cancellable current and previous container log streams
tasks.scope: Add a log adapter that follows container output independently of resource watches.
acceptance: Support selected regular/init containers, tail/since options, timestamps, previous logs, and normal end-of-stream.
Handle chunk boundaries, long lines, partial UTF-8, disconnects, deleted pods, and permission failures explicitly.
Cancellation closes connections; queues and retained data are bounded; retry behavior documents possible duplicates.
tasks.verification: Contract-test chunking/encoding, abrupt disconnects, previous-container errors, cancellation, and bounded memory.

tasks.title: Build the log viewer with pause, follow, search, and bounded scrolling
tasks.scope: Display usable streaming logs while keeping terminal input responsive.
acceptance: Container selection, previous/current mode, timestamps, wrap, search, and follow/pause controls are visible and keyboard accessible.
Scrolling back disables forced follow; returning to follow is explicit; a bounded buffer clearly reports truncated history.
Render in batches, escape untrusted terminal controls, and close streams on exit/context change.
Track timestamps, wrap, head/tail/time windows, clear/mark, column lock, fullscreen and save/copy actions from the audit; later export/clipboard enhancements link to their owning issues.
tasks.verification: Pilot-test scroll/follow transitions, search, resize, hostile output, and stream cleanup; replay a high-volume synthetic stream.

tasks.title: Implement explicit-target subprocess and terminal handoff services
tasks.scope: Create the shared runner for kubectl, editors, and later plugins.
acceptance: Use argument vectors and explicit kubeconfig/context/namespace; validate executable availability and capture targets before awaiting.
Distinguish captured-output processes, background sessions, and foreground terminal handoff with typed outcomes.
Restore terminal state and clean up children on success, exception, Ctrl-C, cancellation, and parent shutdown.
tasks.verification: Test hostile argument values, missing executables, exit statuses, interruptions, and repeated PTY handoffs; command construction meets 100% coverage.

tasks.title: Provide interactive exec with container selection and reliable return
tasks.scope: Open a real container shell through Textual suspension and kubectl exec.
acceptance: Select the exact pod/container/context/namespace and a configured shell; support multiple containers and explain unavailable shells.
Keyboard input, terminal resizing, Ctrl-C, and full-screen programs pass through the real terminal.
Exit or failed exec restores the previous resource view; deleted pods, permissions, and missing kubectl yield actionable errors.
tasks.verification: Run fake-kubectl argument tests and real PTY/kind exec tests covering resize, interruption, failure, and repeated enter/exit.

tasks.title: Manage port-forward sessions and their lifecycle
tasks.scope: Start, inspect, stop, and clean up explicitly targeted pod/service port forwards.
acceptance: Validate mappings and collisions, bind loopback by default, and report readiness from the actual process.
List active sessions with context/resource/ports/status; expose deliberate stop and context-switch behavior.
Failures, resource deletion, app exit, and repeated start/stop leave no orphan processes or listeners.
tasks.verification: Test occupied ports, invalid mappings, startup failure, process death, context switching, and actual network forwarding in kind.

tasks.title: Add aggregated logs and structured-output controls
tasks.scope: Follow multiple containers or workload pods with identifiable, searchable output.
acceptance: Prefix every line with source identity; add/remove streams as workload pods change with a documented concurrency limit.
Offer plain/JSON display, source filtering, and sanitized export without freezing the UI.
Document ordering/clock limitations, cap per-source and aggregate buffers, and close every stream when leaving.
tasks.verification: Test interleaving, pod churn, bad JSON, slow/noisy sources, timestamp differences, cancellation, and aggregate memory bounds.

tasks.title: Create guarded mutation services and read-only mode
tasks.scope: Centralize Kubernetes modifications before adding write actions to resource views.
acceptance: Read-only mode blocks application writes and state-changing commands through a common guard.
Confirmation shows captured context, namespace, resource identity, and intended effect; identity is revalidated where needed.
Permission denial, conflict, timeout, and uncertain write outcomes are distinct; retries do not repeat non-idempotent writes blindly.
tasks.verification: Test every guard bypass route, stale-context race, UID replacement, RBAC denial, and uncertain outcome; deterministic guards meet 100% coverage.

tasks.title: Edit manifests with preview, validation, and conflict handling
tasks.scope: Open selected manifests in the configured editor and apply reviewed changes.
acceptance: Use private temporary files with deterministic cleanup and a safe editor argument parser.
Show a diff, validate YAML/resource identity, perform supported dry-run validation, and handle conflicts without silent overwrite.
Cancelled/unchanged edits make no API write; sensitive fields are handled deliberately and never logged.
tasks.verification: Test malformed YAML, editor failure, no-op edits, changed identity, server validation, conflict/retry, and temp-file cleanup.

tasks.title: Implement scale and rollout operations
tasks.scope: Support scaling, rollout restart/status, and explicit rollback for supported workloads.
acceptance: Actions are offered only for applicable resources and capture the intended target.
Validate replica counts and show progress/status from actual API state; cancellation stops monitoring without misreporting server rollback.
Handle HPA conflicts, paused/failed rollouts, unsupported rollback, and permissions with useful messages.
tasks.verification: Test service contracts plus kind deployment scale/restart/status/rollback, forbidden writes, and timeout/cancellation.

tasks.title: Implement deletion and Job/CronJob operations
tasks.scope: Add deliberate delete/batch-delete, Job creation from CronJobs, and suspension controls.
acceptance: Deletion confirms identity, scope, propagation/grace options, and batch count; read-only mode applies.
CronJob trigger and suspend/resume use supported API semantics and report created resource identity.
Partial batch results, finalizers, resource replacement, permission failures, and ambiguous timeouts remain visible.
tasks.verification: Test mixed batch outcomes, stale UIDs, finalizers, denied operations, duplicate trigger prevention, and real batch API fixtures.

tasks.title: Add deliberate ConfigMap and Secret inspection/editing
tasks.scope: Provide configuration inspection and explicit secret reveal/copy operations.
acceptance: Secret values are hidden by default; reveal/copy are explicit scoped user actions with clear state.
Handle text/binary data and base64 errors without leaking content to logs, snapshots, exceptions, or support bundles.
Editing preserves object identity and uses the common conflict/read-only/mutation flow.
tasks.verification: Use synthetic secret fixtures to test reveal lifecycle, clipboard errors, binary values, redaction across outputs, and guarded edits.

tasks.title: Implement configurable themes and accessible terminal presentation
tasks.scope: Register built-in/custom Textual themes with validated persistent configuration.
acceptance: Users can preview/select themes and save global/context preferences with predictable precedence.
Color is not the only indicator of status; low-color and narrow-terminal fallbacks remain readable.
Invalid theme values recover with an actionable error and preserve working settings.
Provide original KubeRich about/branding content and an opt-in version notice; startup works offline and no external check is required.
tasks.verification: Test theme precedence, invalid files, live switching, contrast/status cues, and representative terminal snapshots.

tasks.title: Configure hotkeys, aliases, and resource views
tasks.scope: Expose user-configurable navigation keys, aliases, column visibility/order, and sorting.
acceptance: Validate reserved keys, conflicts, recursive/ambiguous aliases, and per-resource applicability.
Persist column order/visibility/width and typed sort preferences with schema migrations.
Help and command completion reflect effective configuration; invalid overrides leave the UI navigable.
tasks.verification: Test conflicts, migration/precedence, unknown resource fields, input focus, and custom-view persistence.

tasks.title: Define and load the external plugin contract
tasks.scope: Implement validated plugin manifests, resource scopes, hotkeys, and selected-resource variables.
acceptance: Document command/arguments/environment, scopes, foreground/background behavior, confirmation, and working-directory rules.
Load only configured user plugin locations; cluster objects/current-directory files cannot register executable commands automatically.
Context/resource variables are captured explicitly; malformed or conflicting manifests are rejected with useful messages.

Cover plugin shortcut override, confirmation, dangerous classification, output behavior, per-context directory loading, braced variables/COL fields and typed string/number/bool/dropdown inputs with validation and cancellation.
tasks.verification: Test manifest schema, scope resolution, precedence, hostile variable values, key collisions, and deliberate plugin discovery.

tasks.title: Execute plugins with bounded output and owned process cleanup
tasks.scope: Run configured plugin commands through the shared process and terminal services.
acceptance: Respect configured foreground/background mode and explicit confirmation; represent plugins as unsandboxed local commands.
Read-only mode disables plugins unless an explicit trusted read-only classification is configured; arbitrary plugins cannot be inferred safe.
Limit captured output, redact context-sensitive data, expose exit status/cancellation, and clean up owned processes.
tasks.verification: Test successful/failing commands, malformed environments, noisy output, cancellation, terminal restoration, and read-only gating.

tasks.title: Document and test plugin compatibility and example workflows
tasks.scope: Publish a precise supported plugin schema and useful original examples.
acceptance: Document which K9s plugin configuration fields/variables are compatible, translated, or unsupported; do not claim drop-in compatibility without tests.
Provide tested examples for a resource inspection command, an interactive command, and a background workflow.
Validate examples automatically and document required executables, trust assumptions, and error behavior.

Classify every bundled upstream plugin in the pinned inventory, document external dependencies and free alternatives, and provide tested translation fixtures; third-party tool features are not falsely claimed as native capabilities.
tasks.verification: Run example manifests against synthetic selected-resource fixtures and harmless test executables; check compatibility mapping and documentation.

tasks.title: Implement the complete launch CLI and diagnostic command contract
tasks.scope: Implement all launch, connection, impersonation, and presentation flags enumerated in docs/k9s-cli.md; expose only behavior that actually works in the milestone.
acceptance: Initial release supports help, version, info, --context, --kubeconfig, --namespace/-n, --all-namespaces/-A, --command/-c, --readonly, --write, --refresh/-r, log destination/level, request timeout, cluster/user overrides, impersonation, token and TLS certificate overrides.
Document flag/env/file precedence, mutually exclusive flags, aliases and exit codes. A later-feature flag returns a precise unavailable error until its owning task ships; it never silently succeeds.
Read-only mode blocks shell/attach and every mutating path through shared services, including commands invoked without a UI shortcut; defaults verify TLS and credentials never enter diagnostics.
tasks.verification: Table-driven CLI tests for every audited flag, help snapshots, precedence, invalid combinations, repeated groups, missing files, secret redaction, and read-only bypass attempts.

tasks.title: Qualify EKS authentication and credential refresh
tasks.scope: Support EKS kubeconfig exec credentials through the existing AWS CLI without embedding cloud credentials or provisioning clusters.
acceptance: Honor kubeconfig exec API versions, args/env, AWS profiles/roles and externally established SSO sessions; use aws eks get-token through its declared exec entry.
Refresh expiring tokens without leaking credentials or freezing the UI; explain missing AWS CLI, expired SSO, denied role and API authorization failures separately.
Verify the same identity/overrides reach both API and kubectl subprocess paths; publish cloud qualification evidence honestly.
tasks.verification: ExecCredential contract fixtures cover token expiry, refresh concurrency, role/profile env, invalid JSON and cancellation; opt-in real EKS smoke uses a maintainer-provided test cluster.

tasks.title: Qualify AKS Entra and Azure kubelogin authentication
tasks.scope: Support AKS kubeconfig exec authentication using Azure kubelogin and externally established Azure identities.
acceptance: Cover azurecli, devicecode, service-principal and workload-identity credential contracts without implementing a parallel identity store.
Interactive authentication has explicit terminal handoff/retry; noninteractive sessions fail clearly instead of hanging; distinguish missing kubelogin, expired login, tenant and RBAC failures.
Support exec v1/v1beta1 as appropriate to the SDK, expiration refresh and certificate/token results; unsupported SDK behavior is fixed in the adapter with contract tests.
tasks.verification: Use stub kubelogin commands to test supported modes, expiry, environment, cancellation, redaction and non-TTY behavior; real AKS certification requires an opt-in test tenant.

tasks.title: Qualify generic kubeconfig, GKE, OIDC, proxy and authentication transport
tasks.scope: Close client-go interoperability gaps in Python and keep SDK and delegated tools on the same effective connection.
acceptance: Test merged KUBECONFIG files, relative cert/key paths, embedded certs, token files, exec credentials, gke-gcloud-auth-plugin and external OIDC helpers.
Apply server/proxy/TLS settings and repeated impersonation groups consistently to browsing, logs, exec, Helm and port forwarding; temporary derived config is permission-restricted and cleaned up.

Publish exact supported ExecCredential interactiveMode/provideClusterInfo behavior and any unsupported legacy auth-provider mode with a migration path; do not silently fall back to a different identity.
tasks.verification: HTTPS fake-API and fake-exec contracts test proxy, TLS failures, authorization, refresh races and effective subprocess context; optional GKE smoke, never the current user cluster.

tasks.title: Complete navigation, filtering, scrolling and remote clipboard behavior
tasks.scope: Close the audited table and text interaction surface beyond the first usable browser.
acceptance: Support command history/back-forward/last command, completion, inverse regex, fuzzy, labels/fields, namespace favorites, errors-only and wide-column toggles, selection ranges and typed sorting.
Provide horizontal/vertical scrolling, page/home/end keys, mouse opt-in, breadcrumbs/header/fullscreen toggles, Unicode width handling and stable focus during live updates.
Copy names/namespaces/text with native and OSC52 backends, explicit user intent and payload bounds; support SSH/tmux without interpreting remote text as terminal controls.
tasks.verification: Pilot behavioral tests plus PTY resize/Unicode/SSH/tmux transcripts cover every mapped action; fuzz regex/filter input with bounded evaluation to prevent UI stalls.

tasks.title: Attach to containers and transfer files with explicit targets
tasks.scope: Add kubectl attach and kubectl cp workflows with selected init/regular/ephemeral container identity.
acceptance: Restore terminal state on attach success, EOF, signals and failure, and preserve exit status.
Transfer uploads/downloads using explicit local and remote paths; show overwrite/size/destination intent, explain tar requirements, and never construct shell command strings.
Read-only gates block attach/uploads; downloads require explicit destination and handle traversal/symlink/overwrite risks; cancelled copies leave a clear partial-file state.
tasks.verification: Use disposable pod round trips for small/binary/space-containing files, missing tar and interrupted copies; PTY tests verify attach signals and restoration.

tasks.title: Implement FastForward presets and port-forward transport compatibility
tasks.scope: Support named/numeric ports, multi-forward presets, configurable addresses and K9s-style annotations.
acceptance: Parse documented port-forward annotation syntax including container names and local/remote ports; expose user-confirmed automatic-start preferences.
Annotations from a cluster cannot silently open a listener: automatic forwarding requires explicit local opt-in, loopback defaults and collision validation.
Cover WebSocket/SPDY kubectl transport selection, reconnect state, service-to-pod changes and lifecycle cleanup; feature env names are documented.
tasks.verification: Parse fixtures for every annotation form; real kind forwards check collisions, cancellation, transport failure, remote binding opt-in and stale context events.

tasks.title: Browse, inspect and roll back Helm releases
tasks.scope: Use an optional Helm executable behind a typed adapter for release list/status/values/manifest/history and rollback/uninstall.
acceptance: Display releases across allowed namespaces, revision history, values and manifests with secret-aware defaults; identify supported Helm versions/storage drivers.
Rollback to a selected revision and uninstall require target confirmation and read-only enforcement; handle hooks, timeout and failed/partial releases.
Pass effective context/namespace/identity securely; missing Helm is an actionable feature-specific error.
Include chart notes, user-supplied versus all values, and uninstall keep-history semantics in the compatibility contract.
tasks.verification: Install an original tiny chart in kind, upgrade twice, inspect and roll back; contract tests cover redaction, CLI JSON parsing, missing executable and failures.

tasks.title: Browse local manifests and apply/delete with Kustomize awareness
tasks.scope: Implement the local directory workflow with YAML inspection, editing, rendered Kustomize output, preview and guarded apply/delete.
acceptance: Navigate directories without automatically executing files or remote Kustomize plugins; document symlink and allowed-root handling.
Show rendered resources, namespace/context and server-side dry-run/diff before applying; surface admission errors and per-resource partial outcomes.
Deletion requires explicit resource preview; read-only blocks writes; external editor uses owned terminal handoff.
tasks.verification: Temporary directory fixtures and kind cover multi-document YAML, nested kustomization, malformed files, denial, conflicts, partial apply, deletion and cancellation.
